passage:
Before graduation, students were allowed to write messages on each other's uniforms. Most wrote names, jokes, and short wishes.
Maggie did not want anyone to write on hers. She wanted to keep it clean.
But on the last day, her best friend wrote a tiny message inside the sleeve: "Remember the person you were here."
Maggie was not angry. The words were hidden, but she knew they were there.
Years later, she found the uniform in a box. It no longer fit, and the cloth had turned yellow. But the small message remained.
A uniform is usually meant to make students look the same. Maggie's old uniform had become different because it carried her own memories.
